title: Fatima, 1917
hookLine: three shepherd children and a call to prayer and penance

cards: A town official in Portugal loads some children into his carriage. They are shepherds from the hamlet of Aljustrel, near Fatima: Lucia and her cousins Francisco and Jacinta.

For months they have said that a lady from heaven appears to them on the thirteenth of each month, and crowds now follow them to the field. The official is not a believer, and his government is suspicious of the Church.
He wants the crowds gone and the children's secret out. Instead of taking them to the field, he takes them to his town and locks them up.

teach.b: Stay with those few days. First, the message. The children said the lady asked them to pray the rosary every day for peace and the end of the war, and to do penance, small sacrifices offered for others.
Europe was at war, and Portuguese soldiers were in it. Second, the pressure.
In Lucia's later memoirs, the official questioned them, and when they refused to tell what the lady had confided, he threatened them with death. They were frightened. They still wouldn't tell.
Third, the cell. Lucia recalled that they were put in a room with the town's prisoners. Jacinta was crying for her mother.
Then the children knelt and began the rosary, and some of the prisoners knelt and prayed with them: grown men in a jail, following children through the Hail Mary. Fourth, the outcome.
The children were sent home, and they said the lady came again a few days later, in a different spot.
In the end the Church judged the appearances worthy of belief; Catholics are free to accept them or not, since the Church calls such events private revelations.
At the center is a prayer older than Fatima, the angel's words in Luke's Gospel, in the Douay-Rheims, "Hail, full of grace, the Lord is with thee: blessed art thou among women."
This week ran through a freed slave, an heiress, an immigrant, a little book, children at the altar, a desert brother, and now children praying in a jail.

how: Catholics keep Our Lady of Fatima on 13 May; pilgrims go to the shrine at Fatima, and in parishes people pray the rosary together, often adding a prayer for peace.

games.q: you're Lucia, locked in a room with prisoners. an official has threatened you to make you tell a secret. what do you do?
o: kneel with your cousins and pray the rosary.
try to escape through a window.

practice: A whole rosary won't fit here, so take a small piece of it. Bring to mind one place at war right now; if you pray, say the Hail Mary slowly, once or a few times, for the people there, on beads or on your fingers.
If you don't, hold that place in silence and wish its people safety and an end to the fighting.
